2. Aggrieved by the quantum of the compensation awarded and exoneration of the Insurance Company, the claimant in M.V.C.No.1130/2012 on the file of the Fast Track Court-I and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mysore has preferred this appeal.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. On 13.10.2012 at 7.30 p.m. when the appellant was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing No.KA-45-J-7681 as pillion rider along with one Nagegowda, tractor bearing Registration No.KA-09 TR/E 5295/11-12 hit the said motorcycle near tank bund road, Mavanuru Village within the limits of Saligrama Village, K.R.Nagara Taluk, Mysore District.
In the accident, the appellant sustained grievous injuries.
Respondent No.1 was the driver, respondent No.2 was the registered owner and respondent No.3 was the Insurer of the offending tractor.
4. The appellant was treated in JSS Hospital, Mysore and Mahadeshwara Nursing Home.

He filed M.V.C.No.1130/2012 against the respondents before the Fast Track Court-I and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mysore claiming compensation of Rs.18,00,000/- from the respondents on the ground that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the tractor by respondent No.1.

entities.text: Fast Track Court-I and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mysore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He further claimed that due to the injuries suffered in the accident, he has suffered permanent physical disability.
5. The respondents contested the petition denying rashness and negligence on the part of respondent No.1, age, occupation and income of the appellant.
They claimed that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle bearing No.KA-45-J-7681 by the appellant himself.
Respondent No.3 claimed that the driver of the tractor i.e. respondent No.1 was not holding valid driving licence at the time of the accident, therefore it was not liable to pay the compensation.
6. The Tribunal on recording the evidence and on hearing the parties, by the impugned award held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the tractor by respondent No.1.

However, the Tribunal held that as respondent No.1 was not holding valid driving licence,
respondent No.3 Insurer is not liable to indemnify the damages.

The Tribunal held that in the Giriraje Urs vs Satheesh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120295799/
2 accident, the appellant had suffered one grievous injury of cloud fracture of right tibia and two simple injuries and his movement was restricted for three months.
7.

sentences.text: The Tribunal relying on the evidence of PW.2 the doctor though considered permanent physical disability of the appellant at 11%, awarded global compensation of Rs.40,000/- on the head of pain and sufferings and disability.

The Tribunal in all awarded Rs.1,43,000/- on different heads as per the table below:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in Rs.
 1. Pain and Sufferings and for 40,000/-
 disablement  2. Conveyance 3,000/-
 3. Attendant charges and nourishing 4,000/-
 food  4. For medical expenses 71,400/-
 5. For loss of income during the period 12,000/-
 of treatment  6. Future medical expenses 10,000/-
 7. For discomfort and loss of amenities 2,600/-
 of life  Total 1,43,000/-
 8.
Sri S.A.Saboor, learned Counsel for the appellant submits that the award of global compensation of Rs.40,000/- is incorrect.
He further submits that the income considered by the Tribunal is on lower side.

Relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pappu v. Vinod Kumar Lamba1 he submits that even in the absence of valid driving licence, the insurer has to indemnify the damages and recover from respondent No.2.

9. Sri K.Suryanarayana Rao, learned Counsel for respondent No.3 justifies the impugned award on the ground that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and Insurer was not liable to pay the compensation.
10.
The respondents have accepted the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Tractor by respondent No.1 and with regard to the age of the victim.
11. At the time of accident, the appellant was aged 28 years.
According to him he was an agriculturist and labour.
There was no proof of his income.
Having regard to his age and nature of work and Giriraje Urs vs Satheesh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120295799/
3 other evidence adduced by (2018) 3 SCC 208 him, the Tribunal should have taken the notional income at Rs.7,000/- per month.
12. The Tribunal's findings that the appellant had suffered 11% permanent injury is not under challenge.
The applicable multiplier is 17.
Hence the compensation payable on the heads of loss of future earning have computed based on that, which comes to Rs.1,57,080/- (Rs.7,000 x 11/100 =770 x 12 x 17).
13. The Tribunal has taken the laid up period of the appellant for three months.
Therefore compensation payable on the head of loss of income during the laid up period comes to (7,000x3)=Rs.21,000/-.
The compensation on the head of Medical expenses was awarded based on the medical records that does not call for any interference.
Conveyance charges, attendant charges awarded by the Tribunal are also not under challenge and needs to be maintained.
14. According to PW.2, the appellant had to undergo another surgery for removal of the implantation.
Therefore, compensation awarded on the head of further medical expenses needs to be enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.
15. Considering the nature of the injuries, compensation awarded on the head of loss of amenities is on the lower side, that needs to be enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.

Therefore just compensation is as follows:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in Rs.
 1. Loss of future earning 1,57,080/-
 2. Loss of Conveyance 3,000/-
 3. Attendant charges and 4,000/-
 Nourishment  4. Medical expenses 71,400/-
 5. Loss of income during the laid up 21,000/-
 period  6. Future medical expenses 20,000/-
 7. Loss of amenities 10,000/-
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pappu's case referred to supra, respondent No.3 is liable to indemnify the damages and recover the same from respondent No.2.
The order of the Tribunal needs to be modified accordingly.

Therefore the following:
ORDER
The appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned award is modified as follows:

(i) The appellant/claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,86,480/- with interest thereon at 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of the petition till its realization.

(ii) Respondent No.3 shall deposit the said amount before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this award and recover the same from respondent No.2.
(iii) On such deposit, the Tribunal shall release the amount to the appellant/claimant.
